text:
maria: Quick sync — I'm proposing a compacting change for console analytics envelopes to save storage and improve query perf. Primary idea: replace freeform profile_attrs + ui_labels + long cost blobs with references and small enums. Target ~25-35% storage reduction.

alex: High level sounds good. Which exact keys are considered critical for billing/routing and which can become references?

maria: Critical: route_id, tenant_id, ts, tokens_generated, model_name/variant, billing_keys (currency/unit_rate/model_bucket). Candidates to reference/compact: profile_attrs -> profile_id, ui_labels -> label_mask_id, cost_estimate_meta -> cost_summary(3 fields), raw_prompt -> remove except for sampled/eval traffic. user_agent can be hashed.

simon: Profile_ids imply building a profiles table and backfilling. What's the ingest path?

maria: Plan: dual-write for 2 weeks. Ingest v2 writes compact envelope; ingest v1 continues to write legacy envelope concurrently. Read layer supports both shapes with a compatibility shim. After steady state, run targeted backfills for hot route shards. Full rewrite optional later.

priya: We can't lose signal for evals and QA. Many alert rules depend on prompt snippets and profile attrs.

maria: We'll keep raw_prompt for eval=true and a 0.5% random sample. Also keep full attrs for flagged QA routes. Default path uses profile_id.

alex: How will console queries work for saved dashboards expecting profile_attrs JSON?

dave: Console API should expand profile_id -> attrs on the fly. We'll add a cache layer in console service to avoid DB joins for every request. Also provide a temporary compatibility endpoint for legacy clients.

simon: Backfill approach I suggest: populate profiles table using a grouped extract of distinct profile_attr hashes, then update events for top-N routes using batched updates. Pseudo SQL:

-- create profiles from distinct attrs
INSERT INTO profiles (profile_hash, attrs)
SELECT md5(attrs::text), attrs
FROM events
WHERE attrs IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY attrs
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;

-- then in batches: update events set profile_id = profiles.id, profile_attrs = NULL where md5(profile_attrs::text) = profiles.profile_hash;

maria: Good. We'll only backfill top 5% routes initially. Others will use read-adapter to expand.

priya: Monitoring & canary plan?

maria: Canary ingest v2 at 20% first. We'll run a golden-query set (top-50 dashboard queries) against both shapes and diff counts/sums/sample rows. Abort if >0.5% divergence. Track metrics: ingest 5xx rate, console p95/p99 latency, profile-resolution-rate, profile-miss-rate.

ingest-bot: canary-deploy: ingest-service:v2 started on cluster-us-east-1 (20% traffic).

alex: Versioning: add envelope.schema = "analytics.v2" and keep analytics.v1 for legacy. Reads default to v2 but support query param legacy=true. Feature flag to turn on/off compacting.

dave: Ops ask: don't change retention yet. If compacting hits targets we can revisit retention and cost model. Also need to check compaction impact on hotspotting for partition keys.

simon: One more: since label_mask_id is a bitset id, we need deterministic mapping and migration for existing label sets. We'll build a label-sets table and backfill similarly.

priya: Docs & support: I'll draft migration notes and a support playbook listing common failing queries and fixes (eg: replace profile_attrs->profile_id JOIN snippet).

maria: Timeline draft: Week A: RFC + PR + canary test infra. Week B: Canary 20% + golden queries. Week C: Dual-write 100% + run backfill for hot routes. Week D-E: Dashboard shim rollout + monitor. Week F+: decide on full rewrite.

alex: I'll own the console read-adapter shim and the compatibility endpoint. Simon owns backfill jobs and profiles schema. Priya: you lead docs and monitoring sets.

dave: Infra ok with capacity for backfill windows, but need schedule to avoid peak hours.

priya: Will coordinate post with product, analytics, support. Will include a list of dashboards that must be validated.

maria: I'll open the RFC and a tracking ticket. Any critical objections?

dave: No blockers from infra. Keep us posted on the canary metrics.

ingest-bot: canary-deploy: ingest-service:v2 canary bumped to 50% on cluster-us-east-1.
